meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French-influenced, with Islamic Sharia as a constitutional source of legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982; in force 1992)
Egypt-United States Income Tax Convention (signed 1980; in force 1982)
Egypt-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (1975) and United Kingdom-Egypt Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 2021)
Egypt-European Union Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement (in force 2004)

COMESA Common Investment Area (Egypt is a COMESA member state)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering (Kafh Ghasil al-Amwal), as amended by Laws No. 78 of 2003, No. 181 of 2008, No. 36 of 2015 and Law No. 94 of 2015 on Countering Terrorist Financing, together with its Executive Regulations; the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) of the Central Bank of Egypt issues binding Beneficial Owner (UBO) register instructions applicable to all Egyptian juridical persons, enforced through corporate vetting by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 require the founders' declaration to identify the natural-person beneficial owner (direct or indirect ownership or control through any number of intermediate structures) and to maintain and file the UBO register in accordance with EMLCU and GAFI circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel and local signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of each founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarization in the origin country; legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin country; legalization by the Consular Section of the Embassy of Egypt in that country; final attestation by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Cairo may be required, since Egypt is not a State Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the international passport of each individual founding shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the shareholder's state of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (passport copy attested by a notary in the country of issue; legalization by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin country; legalization by the Consular Section of the Embassy of Egypt)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / company extract (certificate of incorporation in force) of any foreign corporate shareholder, issued not earlier than 90 days before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry / commercial register of the corporate shareholder's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (home-country registry certification; legalization by the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalization by the Consular Section of the Embassy of Egypt; possible final Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation in Cairo)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English-to-Arabic translation of constitutive documents (statutes, articles of association or certificate of incorporation) of each non-Arab corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed sworn translation bureau registered on the Egyptian Ministry of Justice list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by the Egyptian Notary Public and authentication by the translation-certification office, attached to the GAFI establishment file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement of each founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated banking institution of the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for documents originating abroad (notarized bank signature; origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization; Egyptian consular legalization) or notarization by an Egyptian Notary Public if issued by an Egyptian bank branch

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, non-waivable screening of all founders, corporate shareholders, directors and identified UBOs against: (i) the EMLCU domestic judicial asset-freeze and terrorist-designation lists of Egypt; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists (1267/1989/2253 and 1988 regimes); (iii) the OFAC SDN and sectoral sanction lists, given the target payment rails include USD SWIFT wires and credit cards; (iv) the EU consolidated restrictive measures list; and (v) commercial PEP databases. A named PEP (foreign or domestic) triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds documentation. Negative sanctions hits require immediate freezing notification under Law No. 80 of 2002 and a compliance hold on incorporation. Although the commercial model tier is Low_Risk_Standard and simplified customer due diligence may apply to routine non-PEP customers, sanctions and PEP screening can never be simplified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic company-name clearance and incorporation e-services portal (https://www.gafi.gov.eg), linked to the Egyptian Commercial Registry (Al-Sijil Al-Tijari) at the competent GAFI/Commercial Registry office (head office in Cairo and regional branches).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary statutory name must be composed in Arabic script and must carry the Arabic statutory form designation transliterated as 'Sharika Zat Mas'ouliyya Mahdouda' (LLC); the name reserved by GAFI is operative in its Arabic form only. A Latin-script transliteration or a foreign-language commercial trade name may be registered merely as an ancillary designation and never replaces the Arabic statutory name. The proposed Arabic name must be neither identical nor confusingly similar to an existing registered name, reserved name or protected trademark, and must not contain a misleading trade description when rendered in Arabic.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banking (reserved to institutions licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt)
Insurance / Reinsurance (reserved to institutions licensed by the Financial Regulatory Authority - FRA)
Securities / Brokerage / Portfolio Management / Clearing (reserved to FRA-licensed capital-market institutions)
Exchange / Bureau de Change / Money Transfer (currency and remittance activity requires a Central Bank of Egypt license)
Islamic / Shari'a (implies licensed Islamic finance or fund character and requires prior approval of the respective regulator)
Governmental / Ministry / National / Army / Police (implies state affiliation or requires prior consent of the Ministry of Defense or other public authorities)
Foreign sovereign names, internationally protected Olympic or state symbols, and the name 'Arab Republic of Egypt' (require ministerial authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon electronic rejection, the applicant has 30 calendar days to file a written administrative grievance (tazallum) through the GAFI e-complaint channel, attaching a comparative memorandum of law distinguishing the proposed Arabic name from each conflicting registration relied upon by the examiner; GAFI's legal and commercial-registry committee must decide within 15 working days. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may submit a further appeal to the GAFI Chairman within 15 calendar days. Exhaustion of the internal procedure permits annulment proceedings before the competent Economic Court (established under Law No. 120 of 2008) within 60 days of the final administrative refusal, where the court may order the registry to reserve the name if the refusal was arbitrary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical operational address in Egypt evidenced by a notarized lease contract or title deed is mandatory for the Commercial Registry file; a pure virtual office, P.O. box or mail-forwarding address is not eligible for enrolment. A serviced office or managed workspace with a formal commercial tenancy and practical on-site access by authorities is generally accepted for this B2B catalog-e-commerce MRO-supplies activity, provided the statutory books, accounting records and the UBO register are physically accessible or can be produced at the registered address within a short notice window.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 15% probability of a GAFI/Commercial Registry address-verification visit during year one, and approximately 20% probability of an unannounced Egyptian Tax Authority or VAT desk-audit site confirmation; the rate rises to 30% or more if the company files nil revenue, requests VAT refunds in the first two years, or is selected for transfer-pricing audit due to intergroup transactions. Unannounced administrative police licensing checks are not expected for this non-licensed, low-risk retail distribution activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, Executive Regulations Decree No. 96 of 1982, Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (applicable through GAFI), and Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976; LLC provisions in Articles 45–60 and general provisions in Articles 1–19.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop; Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Contract and Articles of Association of the Limited Liability Company (Acte Constitutif / Articles of Association) submitted through GAFI’s single-window registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for Egyptian LLCs under the amended Companies Law; the subscribed quotas must be wholly subscribed and paid in cash or in kind. Cash contributions are deposited in a temporary bank account opened in the company’s name and are released only after registration; no separate escrow account is prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MANAGERS OF EG MRO SUPPLIES LLC. At a meeting on [Date] at [Address], the managers, acting as founders, unanimously resolve: 1. The quota subscriptions described in the Articles of Association are ratified and deemed fully paid from the bank deposit certificate. 2. The registered office at [Address], Cairo, Egypt is adopted as the Company’s statutory seat and address for legal notices. 3. [Name One] is appointed General Manager, and [Name Two] Chief Financial Officer, with authority to operate bank accounts, sign contracts, and conduct ordinary business. 4. The officers are authorised to complete commercial registration, tax registration, municipal licensing, and all related governmental formalities, and to execute all necessary documents. Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Central Company Name Reservation Unit / Ministry of Trade and Industry Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access GAFI’s investor portal or attend the One-Stop Shop. Complete the name reservation form with two alternative Arabic transliterations. Conduct a name search against the Commercial Registry database and the Companies Law restrictions. Provide the proposed corporate object. Retrieve the name reservation clearance certificate before proceeding to notarization.
required_dossiers: Notarized copy of founder national ID or passport
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Power of attorney if an external preparer acts
Proposed Arabic and English company name alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the desired name conflicts, resubmit with alternative Latin and Arabic transliterations. Obtain the written rejection reasons and re-file through the GAFI name committee; administrative objection must be lodged within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office; GAFI-authorised corporate lawyer and legal translator.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed corporate lawyer. Draft and sign the Foundation Contract in Arabic, stating the object as electronic retail trade of industrial maintenance, repair, and operation supplies, the subscribed quotas, initial managers, registered office, and duration. Each founder must sign before a notary public. Obtain official notarial authentication and certified Arabic translations for any foreign-language documents.
required_dossiers: Final Arabic draft of the Articles of Association
Minutes of the founding members’ meeting
Consent letters of the initial managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries an omitted clause, amend and initial the revised pages and re-authenticate. If translation requirements are raised, provide a certified Arabic translation from an accredited translator and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Quota Share Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Bank of Egypt supervised licensed commercial bank (for example, National Bank of Egypt or Commercial International Bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, open a temporary corporate bank account in the company’s name. Deposit the full cash subscription of the issued quotas from each founder. Request a capital deposit certificate or account statement confirming the balance and custodianship. The bank applies standard KYC procedures, including source-of-funds verification for each subscribing member.
required_dossiers: Founder passports and bank KYC forms
Initial deposit application / quota subscription form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit owing to incomplete KYC, provide updated personal identification, proof of address, and source-of-funds documentation. If the name certificate has expired, renew it through GAFI before re-opening the account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application to GAFI for Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop, Cairo.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated Articles of Association, the bank capital deposit certificate, founder ID copies, and the prescribed GAFI incorporation application. Pay the statutory incorporation and commercial registry fees. GAFI reviews compliance with the Companies Law and Investment Law. Upon approval, GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation / Company Establishment Certificate with a company registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association with certified Arabic version
Founder and manager national ID or passport copies
Power of attorney for the filing agent
Declaration of compliance and lawful activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency notice, correct the missing attachments or translations within the specified cure period. If registration is rejected on substantive grounds, appeal to GAFI’s grievance committee within 60 days, or reorganize the corporate object to match the MRO e-commerce scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry, Tax and Social Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); Social Insurance Organisation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the GAFI Certificate of Incorporation to the local Commercial Registry office and complete the Commercial Registry entry under Law No. 34 of 1976. Apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for a tax card and VAT certificate under Law No. 67 of 2016 if taxable supplies exceed the mandatory registration threshold. Register directors and employees with the Social Insurance Organisation.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registrar objects to the activity description, amend the corporate object in a supplementary notarial deed and re-register. If the ETA raises a tax classification mismatch, apply for rectification before the integrated tax office; unresolved delays may be escalated through the GAFI one-stop support desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial License and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Governorate Commercial Licensing Directorate; Ministry of Interior Civil Defense; Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Governorate’s integrated municipal licensing office for a commercial operation license for the warehouse and office. Attach the lease, zoning certificate, building occupancy certificate, and fire safety layout. Schedule a Civil Defense inspection and obtain the fire safety certificate. If the storage area meets the EEAA screening thresholds, submit the environmental compliance registration form. Post the licenses at the registered premises before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate and Commercial Registration certificate
Notarized lease contract and building ownership/zoning letter
Civil defense fire safety layout and inspection request
Manager ID and license applicant power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Civil Defense requires additional fire suppression measures, implement the physical corrections and pay for a re-inspection. If the municipality denies the license on zoning grounds, request a land-use exception or relocate to a compliant commercial/industrial zone; appeal to the Governorate Licensing Grievance Committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry; Governorate Commercial Licensing Directorate for physical warehouse operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Governorate Municipal Commercial License and Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate; Industrial Operation License under Law No. 15 of 2017 is required only if the entity adds on-site manufacturing or assembly.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Initial Environmental Review and registration for storage and e-commerce distribution facilities; full Environmental Impact Assessment is required only if hazardous material storage or industrial production is added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Pure e-commerce MRO warehousing has no significant process discharge. Sanitary wastewater must comply with Law No. 93 of 1962 discharge limits; ambient air quality must comply with Law No. 4 of 1994, Article 38; solid and hazardous waste handling must follow Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020 and EEAA waste manifests where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Certificate under Law No. 20 of 1983 requires fire alarm systems, portable extinguishers, emergency exits, structural load and occupancy review, and annual fire inspection. Occupational safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 is required for employees, including workplace injury prevention, first-aid equipment, and training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance, Arab Republic of Egypt — official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must: (1) obtain commercial registration (CR) issued by the General Authority for Investment and the Ministry of Trade; (2) register with the ETA through the unified electronic tax registration service (Injaz / ETA e-services portal) using the CR, constitutional documents, power of attorney (if applicable), proof of physical premises, and designated bank data; (3) receive a single Tax Identification Number (TIN) that simultaneously serves as the corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and stamp duty identifier; (4) for VAT purposes, verify whether the annual taxable supply value exceeds the mandatory threshold — if so, VAT registration is completed automatically upon TIN issuance; if below the threshold, a VAT registration application is filed separately; (5) after TIN allocation, enrol for the e-invoicing system by obtaining encrypted XML signing certificates and API integration credentials from the ETA e-invoicing platform; (6) appoint a local tax representative and file Form T-1 confirming the registered address, directors, and responsible auditor. Standard processing time for a non-resident-owned LLC is 5–15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Egyptian LLC is a tax-resident juridical person under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 (as amended by Law No. 3/2023). It is subject to corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide income, with a territorial scope rule for non-resident shareholders; dividends paid to non-residents are subject to 10% withholding tax. No fiscal transparency or US-style pass-through treatment is available for LLCs; the LLC itself files, pays, and claims VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity-classification election exists under Egyptian law. Available statutory elections: (a) group consolidation election under Article 51 of Income Tax Law 91/2005 (minimum 90% ownership, binding for five years); (b) tax loss carryforward election (up to five years, subject to ownership continuity conditions); (c) VAT bad-debt relief election for irrecoverable receivables; (d) accelerated depreciation election for machinery and computer hardware; (e) advance pricing agreement (APA) application for transfer pricing certainty; (f) election for services providers to compute foreign-exchange gains/losses on an annual basis. Hybrid mismatch elections under BEPS Action 2 have not been codified as an elective regime in Egypt as of the current law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67/2016, as amended by Law No. 154/2022 and Law No. 3/2023, together with the VAT Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration (EGP 250,000 for voluntary registration); foreign e-commerce and digital service suppliers without a fixed establishment in Egypt are required to register for VAT from the first Egyptian-source supply with no minimum threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide e-invoicing applies to all VAT-registered B2B and B2G transactions. Invoices must be transmitted to the ETA e-invoicing platform as digital documents (UBL 2.1 / XML), signed with the taxpayer's X.509 certificate, validated in near-real-time (within 24 hours of issuance), and returned with an ETA-generated UUID and QR code. There is no physical paper stamping; clearance is electronic only through the ETA fiscal validation firewall. B2C sales are progressively covered by the parallel e-receipt mandate. Integration is performed via REST/OAuth2 APIs over TLS 1.2. Non-compliance or digital-signature bypass triggers automatic VAT re-assessment and monetary penalties ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000 per violation under the amended tax procedure rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 21 of VAT Law 67/2016 for: (i) physical export of goods outside the Egyptian customs territory, evidenced by a valid customs export declaration; (ii) export-related services directly connected to goods (handling, transport, freight, insurance, international inspection/quality certification) provided the proceeds are transferred from abroad in freely convertible currency; (iii) supplies of goods and services to free zones treated as being outside the tax territory. The Egyptian LLC must demonstrate a genuine B2B export contract with a non-resident buyer, actual delivery of the industrial MRO hardware beyond Egyptian borders, and full receipt of the foreign-currency sales price in an Egyptian bank account.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Single Administrative Document (SAD) stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority, including the MASKOUT release certificate
Commercial invoice and B2B MRO catalogue order documentation correlated to the export declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export shipment and matching the stated INCOTERMS
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the receiving Egyptian bank proving that foreign-currency export proceeds were credited in Egypt
ETA Export Zero-Rating Claim Form with the ETA-issued invoice/reference numbers from the e-invoicing platform
Packing list and insurance certificate (required for CIF/CIP terms)
Certificate of Origin (optional for MRO hardware; required only where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and the Central Bank of Egypt jointly reconcile export zero-rated sales against the customs SAD database and bank foreign-currency credit records. If export proceeds are not repatriated to and credited in an Egyptian bank account within 180 days from the customs release date, the zero-rating is retroactively revoked. The ETA will assess the full 14% VAT on gross export turnover, plus statutory delay penalties, plus an additional violation amount of up to EGP 50,000 per incorrect return under Article 34 of VAT Law 67/2016. In fraud or deliberate misstatement cases, Article 35 imposes a fine equal to the tax evaded and terms of imprisonment, as intensified by Law 154/2022, and e-invoicing misdeclarations attract fines of EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000 per false declaration. For corporate income tax purposes, un-repatriated or undocumented export receivables may be recharacterised as deemed distributions to the foreign parent, triggering 10% dividend withholding tax, immediate CIT catch-up, and transfer-pricing penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — البنك المركزي المصري, the sole monetary authority and banking supervisor under Law No. 194 of 2020. FX operations, payment systems, and bank licensing are administered by the CBE, with concurrent oversight by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for inward equity registration and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (MLTFCU) for AML/CFT enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has operated a unified, flexible exchange-rate regime since the CBE decision of 6 March 2024. The Egyptian pound (EGP) is fully convertible at interbank rates for current-account flows — trade, services, profit remittances, and dividend repatriation — with no prior CBE approval for bona fide underlying transactions. Capital-account inflows for foreign equity are liberalized for LLCs, but every foreign-currency receipt must enter through a CBE-licensed bank and be registered with GAFI under the Law on Investment No. 72 of 2017. Dividend, branch-remittance, and liquidation proceeds may be repatriated at the interbank rate upon submission of: (i) audited financial statements, (ii) a tax-clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), and (iii) the bank's FX declaration form. Practical friction is limited to bank-side compliance review queues rather than statutory convertibility ceilings; there is no deposit-holding tenor requirement for non-resident proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: 100% of merchandise export receipts must be repatriated through the Egyptian banking system within 30 days from the date of the bill of lading / air waybill; an extension to 180 days is available only for pre-approved capital-goods and government-procurement contracts with CBE authorization. Mandatory conversion quota: the pre-2024 forced-surrender rule was rescinded by the March 2024 CBE liberalization — exporters may retain the full export value in foreign currency in a CBE-licensed FCY account or convert at the interbank rate. Retention is lawful only where the corresponding customs entry (C21 declaration) is presented to the receiving bank, and utilization of retained FCY is restricted to current-account payments of the same trading business (raw-material imports, trade-finance settlement) to curtail FX fronting and speculative warehousing. The receiving bank must record each repatriation in the CBE consolidated FX database; late receipt is treated as a compliance event requiring an explanatory memorandum to the MLTFCU.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (GAFI/FDI inward remittance) + Operational EGP/USD Current Account
Operational EGP/USD Current Account + Import Settlement Sub-account
Operational EGP/USD Treasury Account + Merchant Card Settlement Account
Multilayer Operational Account (EGP/USD/EUR) + Cross-Border SWIFT Concentration Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Qatar National Bank AlAhli (QNB AlAhli) Egypt

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP/USD Account + LC Disbursement Sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail. Under Law No. 194 of 2020 and the Fintech-Enabling Law No. 5 of 2022, non-resident e-money institutions (EMIs) licensed in the UK/EU or Asia-Pacific are not recognized as banks in Egypt and cannot hold the LLC's EGP or FCY deposits, open SWIFT-branch accounts, or clear Egyptian electronic payments without a CBE license. Legal viability is limited to two permitted configurations: (i) use of a licensed onshore fintech acquirer (e.g., Paymob, Fawry+) as a card-acceptance front-end, with all settlement sweeps landing in a CBE-licensed operational bank account; or (ii) feeder corporate accounts at foreign EMIs for small non-resident receipts which are subsequently swept by SWIFT MT103 into the Egyptian operational account. In both cases, the settlement leg must terminate at a Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory. The general manager and at least one ultimate beneficial owner with a 25% or greater shareholding (or two directors of the LLC's management body) must attend a face-to-face KYC interview at the bank's compliance desk in Egypt. Remote videoconference onboarding is not accepted by Egyptian Tier-1 banks for a newly incorporated LLC with non-resident shareholders. The entity file must include: notarized and apostilled articles of association, commercial registry extraction (السجل التجاري), tax card (البطاقة الضريبية), GAFI investment certificate, certified board resolution for account opening, original passports of all signatories/UBOs, and Arabic translations of all statutory documents where requested. A remotely executed power of attorney cannot substitute for the initial interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pattern mismatch between card-present e-commerce inflows and back-to-back SWIFT export wires: low average order value (AOV) for industrial MRO supplies, inconsistent unit prices, irregular HS-code sequencing, and same-day payout requests to suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-to-end order-to-cash (O2C) dossier: itemized commercial invoices keyed to HS-2022 codes under NAICS 423840 mapping, OEM/distributor authorization letters, unit-cost benchmark reports, transport documents (BL/AWB/CMR) for each shipment, customs C21 declaration prints, internal ERP O2C traceability, and a 12-month transaction analytics report demonstrating that 100% of card and wire receipts match unique purchase orders and invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity in a 100% non-resident-owned Egyptian LLC, raising shell-company, nominee-director, and undisclosed-beneficial-owner red flags under Egypt AML Law No. 80 of 2002.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate-chain certificate tracing every shareholder to the ultimate individual with passport copies and residential proof; signed UBO declaration on the CBE-prescribed template; home-bank reference letters issued by each shareholder's banking institution within six months; CPA-certified source-of-wealth letter for each equity contribution; director questionnaires; and verified negative-news and PEP screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Across-the-book FX fronting / third-party trade intermediation: the bank observes wire proceeds from unrelated foreign payers whose counterparty names do not appear in the LLC's invoice book, a classic exporter-fronting indicator under Egyptian FX regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-integrity package: matching of every receipt to unique invoice and purchase-order numbers; buyer KYC profiles of e-catalog B2B customers (company incorporation extracts and transaction IP/fraud-review logs); CBE export-record references; bonded warehouse stock-movement records for Borg El Arab and Alexandria facilities; logistics service-level agreements with freight forwarders; and a sworn statutory declaration that no third-party payment intermediation or nominee collection is conducted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-corridor exposure: counterparties or settlement corridors touching GCC/MENA and sub-Saharan African jurisdictions that produce OFAC/EU/UN screening hits or false-positive ambiguities, given Egypt's position as a cross-regional remittance hub.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening dossier generated through a recognized provider (Refinitiv World-Check / Dow Jones) with a documented hit-and-elimination rationale for each name; geo-location proof of MRO inventory storage in Egyptian customs-bonded facilities; end-user attestation certificates from low-risk jurisdictions; and a contractual compliance addendum embedding UN/EU/OFAC blocking clauses with automatic list-update monitoring to be countersigned by all material counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the shareholder's corporate bank into a segregated Capital Account held at the chosen CBE-licensed Egyptian bank. The wire must carry the IMF-BPM6-style balance-of-payments reason code for equity subscription in the non-financial corporate sector (capital contribution category), the LLC's GAFI investment registration reference, and the account beneficiary name exactly matching the Egyptian commercial registry extract. Before the funds are credited, the bank requires: (i) a fully cleared KYC/UBO file, (ii) GAFI registration or investment certificate, (iii) a certified board resolution designating Capital Account signatories and the subscribed amount, (iv) a CPA/auditor source-of-funds letter for the specific wire, and (v) the ETA tax-identification confirmation. Upon receipt, the bank either converts the inflow at the interbank reference rate or maintains the FCY balance in the Capital Account at the investor's written election. The account is marked 'restricted — capital injection', reported to GAFI and CBE in the consolidated FX database, and may not be netted against operational trade payments. No inward equity remittance is legally recognized outside a CBE-licensed bank channel.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The treasury clears supplier disbursements on three rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for routine MRO replenishment payments up to approximately USD 50,000 equivalent — the bank verifies the import invoice, customs C21 classification code, and the IMF-style trade reason code (imports of goods) before execution at the interbank offer rate; (2) commercial documentary letters of credit issued via MT700 for bulk procurement tranches, settled through MT202/MT910 reimbursement against compliant presentation (commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate, BL/AWB, and certificate of origin), with a CBE-licensed advising/negotiating bank discounting the supplier's drafts; and (3) inbound B2B card-not-present e-commerce settlement through a licensed onshore acquirer (CIB/NBE/Paymob), which clears card transactions via the Misr Interbank ACH/RTGS infrastructure and nets daily into the LLC's operating account, subject to a standard chargeback reserve. All outbound SWIFT flows must be pre-funded with cleared funds and remain within the bank's sanctioned daily FCY limit framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright EGP/USD FX forwards executed through a CBE-authorized dealer for trade-backed maturities of up to 12 months; naked or speculative forward cover is prohibited.
Onshore EGP/USD FX swaps used to align the liquidity gap between export-receipt inflows and import-payable outflows in the treasury calendar.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on EGP executed through international banks (London/New York desks) referencing the CBE published reference rate — deployed as a fallback hedge when onshore dealer limits are exhausted.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) on a real-exposure basis under an ISDA Master Agreement with an OECD or Egyptian counterparty, subject to CBE derivative eligibility, margin, and trade-documentation requirements.

Plain-vanilla FX options (EGP call / USD put) via CBE-approved derivatives providers for 3- to 6-month distribution or dividend-repatriation cycles, permitted only when supported by documented current-account exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renewal of the Commercial Record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic registry portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year basis: renewal must be completed on or before 31 March of each year; the electronic renewal window opens on 1 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No grace period after 31 March; late renewal triggers administrative fines under Trade Registry Law No. 34 of 1976. Non-renewal for more than 12 months may result in ex-officio strike-off from the Commercial Register and loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statement of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBO Register Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) UBO declaration module; register available on site for inspection by the Anti-Money Laundering Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based, submitted together with the annual Commercial Registry renewal on or before 31 March of each year; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be notified to GAFI within 30 days of the transfer being recorded in the shareholders' register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EGP 20,000 to EGP 1,000,000 under AML Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 13 of 2019; uncorrected UBO data may freeze GAFI e-services and trigger interbank account restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Advance Corporate Income Tax Instalments (Provisional Income Tax Payments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three instalments for calendar-year taxpayers due 15 April, 15 July, and 15 October; final balancing payment is remitted with the annual corporate income tax return on 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid instalments are subject to a 2% monthly default surcharge on the amount in arrears and may trigger an administrative seizure order before the annual return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT Return and Supporting Audited Financial Statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) via the electronic tax filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months from the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delinquency surcharge of 2% of unpaid tax, plus a late-filing penalty of 1% of tax due for each month of delay; persistent non-filing leads to enforced collection, asset attachment, and travel restrictions on responsible managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) VAT Directorate via the electronic VAT portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly: no later than the last day of the month following each tax period. Quarterly election: no later than the 30th day of the month following the calendar quarter, available where annual taxable turnover does not exceed EGP 1,000,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of EGP 1,000 to EGP 20,000 per period; unpaid VAT accrues a 1.5% monthly late-payment charge under Tax Procedure Law No. 14 of 2020, plus enforced collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partners' Resolution Approving the Audited Annual Financial Statements (Annual Meeting or Written Resolution Minutes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory minute book at the registered office; available for inspection by GAFI and ETA tax auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end and before the annual CIT return filing; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold or archive the annual partners' resolution impairs the evidentiary validity of the financial statements before the ETA; managers may become jointly liable for company debts if statutory corporate books are not properly maintained under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or staff exemption: every Egyptian limited liability company must appoint at least one certified public accountant as statutory auditor for each financial year. The audit requirement is imposed by legal form under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, including for dormant or zero-turnover LLCs.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) prepared in Arabic; EAS constitute the local GAAP aligned with IFRS and are mandatory for all LLCs preparing statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers become opposable to third parties only after annotation in the shareholders' register at the registered office. The company must update the UBO register within 30 days of any transfer and transmit the change to GAFI; an annual confirmation statement is signed and filed by 31 March of each year, in tandem with the annual Commercial Registry renewal, certifying the Ultimate Beneficial Owner list as at the preceding 31 December, regardless of whether a transfer occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes Book of Members' and Managers' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,500 per year (representative Cairo registered office and annual agency services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 2,200 per year for a statutory audit of an e-commerce LLC with an active B2B MRO trading book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory free-zone 0% CIT holiday for licensed free-zone enterprises (export-focused) under Investment Law No. 72/2017 and Free Zones Law No. 19/1997; Investment Law tax deduction of 30%-50% of project investment costs, deductible over a maximum of 5 tax years for eligible industrial distribution and logistics projects; regional uplift available for projects in the Suez Canal Economic Zone and Upper Egypt; no further reduced headline rate for a standard Egyptian LLC.
